criteria: make lint passes on the current tree: ruff, mypy strict on src and every brief section 11 import-linter contract report zero violations.
A GPX file outside test fixture folders is ignored by git; every file under tests/fixtures/ and the acceptance fixtures/gpx/ folder stays tracked.
make bootstrap on a clean Mac checkout installs locked Python dependencies and the pre-commit and pre-push hooks.
HYPOTHESIS_PROFILE selects dev (100 examples), ci (1,000, derandomized) or mutation (50, derandomized).
pre-push runs mypy, lint-imports and pytest excluding slow, solver_child and walking_skeleton markers in under five minutes.

steps.name: OR-Tools solver probe in a child process
steps.description: Introduce the TourSolver port (probe contract only) and the OR-Tools adapter whose probe solves the fixed six-node instance twice in a short-lived child process; a failing probe makes the planner degraded-unhealthy with optimizer_unavailable.
criteria: On a healthy host the solver probe solves the fixed six-node instance twice with identical, known-optimal orders, and /api/health reports it ok.
A crashing, hanging or wrong-answering solver child makes /healthz answer 503 with reason optimizer_unavailable while every other endpoint keeps working.
A tour_solver given through ExternalPorts replaces the OR-Tools adapter at the composition root.
OR-Tools is imported only inside adapters.solver, enforced by import-linter contract 7.
The probe adds at most 3 seconds to start-up on the Mac.

steps.implementation_notes:
Slice 00a (the arm64 smoke must prove the aarch64 OR-Tools wheel, D84/D168). Port: TourSolver extends Probeable; in 00a it declares only the probe contract - solve() and incumbent streaming are added at slice 01b (ADR-015), so no stubbed solve. Probe per ADR-011 Amendment 1: fixed 6-node asymmetric instance with one track node and one forbidden arc, solved twice in a short-lived child process (spawn context, bounded timeout), expect the known optimum and identical orders; failure -> degraded, unhealthy, /healthz 503 reason 'optimizer_unavailable' (brief section 7). Keeping OR-Tools out of the main process also protects the idle-RAM guardrail (G1 < 300 MB). Gold fault catalogue (integration, marker solver_child, single-example): child crash, child hang, wrong order. Commit: 'feat(solver): OR-Tools probe in a child process'. steps.name: Multi-stage hardened planner image
steps.description: Write the multi-stage Dockerfile (node build stage, uv-locked Python builder, slim non-root runtime) with digest-pinned bases, OCI labels, healthcheck and a .dockerignore that keeps secrets, data and GPX files out of the build context.
criteria: One Dockerfile builds linux/amd64 and linux/arm64: web built on the build platform, Python installed from uv.lock without dev dependencies, slim runtime.
The container runs as uid 10001, owns /data, declares no volume and has a healthcheck on /healthz.
Every base image and the uv binary are pinned by digest; labels revision, source, created, alembic-head and commit-ts are set.
.dockerignore excludes .git, .data, every .env file, node_modules, tests, docs and GPX files from the build context.
Bytecode is precompiled so the planner can run on a read-only root filesystem, writing only to /data and /tmp.
steps.scenario_name: test_node_stage_runs_on_buildplatform | test_python_installed_with_uv_sync_frozen_no_dev | test_bytecode_is_precompiled | test_base_images_and_uv_are_pinned_by_digest | test_runtime_user_is_10001 | test_no_volume_is_declared | test_oci_labels_are_set | test_dockerignore_excludes_secrets_data_and_gpx | test_healthcheck_targets_healthz
steps.implementation_notes:
Slice 00a, D84/D170/D173/D176. Stage 1 node:22-bookworm-slim@sha256 on $BUILDPLATFORM (npm ci && vite build). Stage 2 python:3.12-slim-bookworm@sha256 builder with uv copied from ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv:<ver>@sha256, `uv sync --frozen --no-dev`, UV_COMPILE_BYTECODE=1; runtime on the same base. The Python digest in D84 is truncated ('e697c818...d337') and the node digest says '<pin at 01a>': resolve and pin both now (the Python base must be the one SPIKE-1R ran in). User 10001; /data created and owned by it; NO `VOLUME /data` (user decision: the 01a scenario 'packaged planner started without its data storage' needs DATA_DIR on the container's overlay root). ENV DATA_DIR=/data, WEB_DIST_DIR=/app/web/dist, ROUTING_PROVIDER=mock (until 06a). CMD uvicorn --factory ... --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8080 --workers 1 (container-internal; host exposure is decided by compose, D174). HEALTHCHECK = Python one-liner on /healthz (30 s interval, 3 retries, 30 s start period). Build args GIT_SHA, COMMIT_TS, ALEMBIC_HEAD (default 'none' until migrations exist at 02-01) -> labels org.opencontainers.image.{revision,source,created}, org.overland.alembic-head, org.overland.commit-ts and ENV PLANNER_GIT_SHA. .dockerignore (D170): .git, .data, .env*, node_modules, tests, docs, *.gpx, .venv, web/dist, mutants. The Mac has no Docker: the step's done-when is the static contract test (plus hadolint if installed); static tests cover the node stage on $BUILDPLATFORM, `uv sync --frozen --no-dev` and UV_COMPILE_BYTECODE=1, while the actual amd64/arm64 builds are checked by CI jobs 5 and 6 (step 01-08) and the read-only-root run by job 7 (step 02-04). The image-level @docker scenario 'Sharing the packaged planner never shares Marco's password' is mapped to 01-09 (CI job 7). Commit: 'build(image): multi-stage non-root planner image'. Crafter stops at the commit; no push.

steps.implementation_notes:
Slice 00a, DEVOPS CI table jobs 1, 2, 4; D86, D161, D162, D168, D169, D170, D178. Triggers: push (all branches), pull_request to main, workflow_dispatch; concurrency ci-${{ github.ref }} (cancel-in-progress except main); docs-only path filter -> lint-docs only. Default permissions contents: read. Caches: setup-uv enable-cache (uv.lock), setup-node npm. Job 2: `npm ci && npx vite build`, PLANNER_TEST_WORKSPACE and DATA_DIR under $GITHUB_WORKSPACE, `df -T` before pytest, HYPOTHESIS_PROFILE=ci, pytest $PENDING_FLAGS -m 'not real_provider and not pi and not walking_skeleton' with coverage total >= 80% (the domain >= 90% gate is switched on at 02-02, when domain code first exists). USER DECISIONS (2026-11-02): PENDING_FLAGS starts empty (02-07 adds --run-pending=slice-00b, 03-10 adds --run-pending=slice-01a), overriding D170's 'today' value; the walking skeleton runs in a separate job-2 step with continue-on-error: true (visible in the summary) until 03-06 makes it blocking. Job 1 per DEVOPS table incl. pip-audit on `uv export --frozen --no-dev` and npm audit --omit=dev --audit-level=high. Job 4: npm ci, vitest, vite build, upload web-dist. dependabot weekly, grouped (actions, uv, npm, docker). The test parses ci.yml with PyYAML and asserts the contract (jobs, needs, triggers, permissions, PENDING_FLAGS use, SHA-pinned actions, runner pins). Commit: 'ci: commit stage with lint, python and web tests'. Crafter stops at the commit; no push.

steps.name: Seeded I1/I2 generator, committed fixtures and golden order
steps.description: Re-creates the SPIKE-1R seeded instance generator as test tooling and commits I1 (dense) and I2 (sparse variant): 60 items (40 tracks, 20 POIs) plus Start 'Casa Marco, Torino' and End 'Briancon', in the fixture contract of the slice-03 binding, with the golden order and its sha256 as the planner finds them at the default budget.
criteria: Generating twice with seed 20261101 writes byte-identical i1-dense.json, i2-sparse.json and i2-sparse.road-map.yaml under fixtures/golden/; each instance has 40 tracks and 20 POIs with unique names, Start 'Casa Marco, Torino' and End 'Briancon' (62 stops), placed from one table of 68 named Western Alps places (Piedmont, Aosta Valley, Hautes-Alpes).

Every track starts at a place and ends 2-40 km away at a seeded bearing; its recorded polyline length is 1.4 times the straight line within 1 %; road distances are those of the offline road map (straight line x 1.3).

The planner accepts I2's road map as MOCK_PLAN at start-up; it lists only pairs between I2's own points and turns about 5 % of I2's required pairs into one-way detours (asymmetric costs); I1 uses the default road map.

Each fixture's expected_order is the 62 stop names, Start first and End last, that the planner returns through its API at the default budget 10,000, and expected_order_sha256 is the sha256 of those names joined by newlines in UTF-8; both are written by the generator's bless command, never by hand, and a different committed order is overwritten only on an explicit re-bless.

'The 60-item plan is the same on every machine' passes locally with --run-pending=slice-03, its time reported; the order hash and the fixture reader have one definition, used by the binding, the golden check and the generator.

The fixtures and the generator's docstring record that the golden is blessed on the current single GLS search (D223), and name the re-bless trigger: any change to the weighting mode, the phase limits, the solver identity (SOLVER_IDENTITY), the default budget or the ortools version (for example 06a/06b two-phase weighting) re-blesses both instances in a commit of its own.

steps.name: Solver child streams incumbents; a crash keeps the best route so far
steps.description: The solve child sends every improving valid route as an incumbent; the parent keeps the last valid one and the poll payload shows it. A child that ends abnormally after an incumbent gives a ready run labelled 'not fully optimised (optimizer failed)' (D223 b; code optimizer_failed), not reproducible (D122). Plan runs gain the run flags of brief section 8 (Alembic 0008).
criteria: While solving, the poll payload's incumbent is null until the first valid route, then {unconfirmed_legs, retraces, objective, found_at_s} of the last valid one; a message that is not a complete tour from Start to End is ignored.

'An optimizer that crashes after finding a route still gives the best route so far' passes: the run is ready with the last incumbent's order, not_fully_optimised optimizer_failed, reproducible false, and its messages carry the label text exactly 'not fully optimised (optimizer failed)' (D223 b, words as D220 e); a crash before any incumbent stays a Failed optimizer_failed run with its exit code or signal logged.

A budget-ended solve is unchanged: reproducible true, not_fully_optimised null, `uv run pytest -q -m golden_order` passes for I1 and I2 with the committed shas, and 'The optimizer ends without any route' stays green (Failed no_valid_route_found at once).

The real child sends only improving incumbents and its final order equals its last incumbent; the guard judges the chosen order and a violation still gives Failed internal_invariant_violation, with no fallback to an earlier incumbent.

Alembic 0007 -> 0008 adds the run flags (reproducible, not_fully_optimised, run time, memo source) to plan_runs, older runs reading reproducible true and no label; the round trip passes; the run detail and list show reproducible and not_fully_optimised; the job log and plan.job.finished carry incumbents, reproducible and not_fully_optimised_reason.

steps.name: Feasibility and optimisation limits from job start
steps.description: FEASIBILITY_LIMIT_S (default 600) and OPTIMISATION_LIMIT_S (default 1800), configurable and measured from pressing Calculate (D41, D58), bound every solve. 'No valid route within the feasibility limit' passes: with FEASIBILITY_LIMIT_S=30 and no incumbent the job ends done with a Failed run, reason timeout, and Marco sees 'No valid route found within the time limit - plan run #N failed' with the new run's number.
Reaching the feasibility limit with an incumbent does not end the solve; it ends at the budget, the optimisation limit or a Stop (ADR-015 state table).

Both limits are read from settings as whole seconds above 0; a feasibility limit above the optimisation limit, or a value that is not a whole number above 0, refuses start-up with health.startup.refused naming the key; compose and .env.example pass both through with their defaults.

No solve child waits without a bound: the parent ends the child (SIGTERM, then SIGKILL after 2 s) at the limit that applies, and a hung child without an incumbent still ends as a Failed timeout run (D200); the separate 600 s constant is gone.

steps.name: Look-up latency, legs found so far, and Stop or limit during the road look-up
steps.description: The offline road map gains a look-up latency (MOCK_PLAN `latency`, brought forward from slice 06a in its minimum form), the poll shows legs_new and legs_cached as legs arrive, and road legs found are kept in memory for the next Recalculate. A Stop or the feasibility limit while legs are fetched ends the job with no run and changes nothing (D43, D151, D157).
criteria: 'Stopping while roads are still being looked up changes nothing' passes: no plan run, 'Stopped - nothing was changed', and the next Recalculate reuses at least as many legs as had been found.

'The feasibility limit reached while roads are still being looked up changes nothing' passes: the job ends timed_out at the limit even while a road-map call is still running, with 'No valid route found within the time limit - nothing was changed', no run, and the legs found kept.

MOCK_PLAN accepts `latency: {answered_at_once_pairs, then_each_call_s}` (numbers of at least 0) and an empty pairs list; once the pairs answered reach the first number every further matrix call waits the second; probe calls are never delayed; a malformed latency refuses start-up naming the file.

Road legs are kept in memory for the planner process's life per provider_id and pair; the poll payload and the job log count legs_new and legs_cached as they arrive, the cached ones before any new call; a late answer to a call that outlived its job never stores a run.
Without latency the golden check and the slice 01b and 02 suites stay green, and a second identical Calculate asks the road map for nothing (legs_new 0, legs_cached equal to legs_total).

steps.name: Leg table and resolver keep levels and 'no road'; the retrace rule has one home; second-pass pairs
steps.description: LegTable and LegResolver carry each leg's level and reason and remember pairs with no road (asked once). A pure domain rule decides, for a track t and a successor j, whether the road leaves t's exit, a retrace is needed, or the arc is forbidden; it is the only definition used by the model, the assembler and the guard. The job asks the retrace candidates' second pair entry(t) -> entry(j) only where the first came back with no road (ADR-017 section 2).
criteria: LegTable answers a pair's level and reason, and whether any road connects it; a pair known to have no road is distinct from a pair nobody asked (that stays a KeyError); identical points are Confirmed 0 m 0 s.
LegResolver keeps level, reason and no-road per provider_id and pair for the process's life; a no-road answer is cached and never asked again; the legs counters keep new + cached = total.

The retrace rule (one pure function in the domain, no I/O) gives, for track t and successor j: 'road' when exit(t) -> entry(j) is connected at any level; 'retrace' when it is not and entry(t) -> entry(j) is connected; 'forbidden' otherwise; a POI as t, and a loop track whose exit equals its entry, never give 'retrace'; identical points (exit(t) equal to entry(j)) are 'road' (0 m, nothing to drive).

The job asks the second-pass pairs after the first pass resolves and only for the (t, j) whose first pair has no road; a project without a no-road pair asks exactly the pairs it asks today (request count unchanged, 07-01 pin green); the number of second-pass pairs is noted for plan_job_log.second_pass_pairs.

steps.name: Solver model: retrace arcs and the lexicographic order (Unconfirmed, retraces, road km)
steps.description: The tour model gains retrace arcs and weights so that one search orders plans by fewest Unconfirmed legs (a retrace counts as one), then road metres only (retrace km are reported and counted off-road but are not in the objective; there is no retrace penalty: W2 already makes fewer retraces win). The model also carries the real (unweighted) tables from which the reported objective and the Unconfirmed and retrace counts are read. A model with only Confirmed legs is unchanged, to the byte.
criteria: Arcs follow the retrace rule of 07-03: an exit-side road arc at its level; a retrace arc t -> j for a track t with exit(t) -> entry(j) having no road and entry(t) -> entry(j) connected; otherwise no arc; no arc ever arrives at a track's exit and a POI never has a retrace arc.

Arc cost: a Confirmed arc costs its plain metres; every other arc costs W1 * (Unconfirmed legs on it, a retrace counting one, plus 1 more if its entry -> entry leg is Unconfirmed) + W2 * (retraces on it) + c, with c the arc's metres, and for a retrace arc c = the metres of entry(t) -> entry(j) only (neither the track's length nor any penalty: the third criterion is road km, ruling 2026-11-10); W2 and W1 are computed per model from the largest c and the number of arcs of a tour as ADR-016 section 4 gives them, and every cost fits an int64 for 72 stops with legs up to 3,000 km.

Property over generated small models (up to 6 items, random levels and no-road pairs): the order the model's cost ranks first is the lexicographic minimum of (Unconfirmed legs, retraces, road metres only) over every order (brute force on the matrix, no OR-Tools); where two orders tie on all three, either may win; a saving in km never buys an extra Unconfirmed leg or retrace. Criterion 2 in isolation (a unit test, since scenario 'An order with fewer retraces wins over a shorter order' cannot show it): two orders with the same number of Unconfirmed legs, one with a retrace and one with an Unconfirmed road leg 30 km longer and no retrace: the one without the retrace wins.

The model carries the real tables (road metres per arc, Unconfirmed legs per arc, retraces per arc) and describes any order as (road metres, Unconfirmed legs, retraces) with no weight in it: retrace km are not in the objective, so a plan with one retrace has road metres = the road legs' metres exactly (the track's length is reported and counted off-road in 07-06 only).

For a model of Confirmed legs only the cost matrix equals today's, cell for cell: the 07-01 pins of I1 and I2 pass and `uv run pytest -q -m golden_order` passes unchanged; the fingerprint scheme leads with fp2 and hashes the weights; a per-field test (D124) shows that changing each input alone (the scheme, W1, W2, the weighting mode, one arc's level, the presence of a retrace arc) changes the fingerprint, and equal models give equal fingerprints; a Confirmed-only model's fingerprint differs from fp1's (one recalculation of existing projects, noted).

A real OR-Tools child (solver_child) given a small model with a retrace arc returns the lexicographic optimum, and its incumbents decode to the same counts the brute force gives; a real-child property over sparse models of at most 12 items (solver_child, 20 cases) finds the brute-force optimum of (Unconfirmed legs, retraces) and reports its road-km gap; the solve time of a sparse 60-item variant of I2 on the Mac (dead ends at 10 percent of tracks, generated on the fly, not committed) is reported next to I2's, as information.

steps.name: Valhalla in the compose stack: profile routing, caps, internal network, never published
steps.description: Adds the routing engine to deploy/compose.yaml as designed in ADR-013 Amendment 3 (D234): service `valhalla` in profile `routing`, the internal `routing` network, the volume overland_valhalla-data mounted by tileset subpath, caps and healthcheck. The planner and planner-perf join `routing`. The Pi tooling turns the profile on whenever routing.env exists, and a planner deploy brings valhalla to its definition without ever failing on it.
criteria: deploy/compose.yaml defines `valhalla`: image `ghcr.io/valhalla/valhalla-scripted:3.9.1-arm64@sha256:f182f45e9e71cbe737e6c394d68808c67a7bd12e2a4cc47c4aba864de77ecdc6` (overridable as `${VALHALLA_IMAGE:-...}` for an amd64 PC), `profiles: [routing]`, networks `[routing]` only, no `ports`, environment serve_tiles=True, use_tiles_ignore_pbf=True, force_rebuild=False, server_threads=2, update_existing_config=False, build_admins/build_time_zones/build_elevation/build_transit=False, `cpus: 2`, `mem_limit: 4g`, `memswap_limit: 4g`, `oom_score_adj: 500`, `restart: unless-stopped`, `security_opt: [no-new-privileges:true]`, `pids_limit: 512`, json-file logging 10m x 3, healthcheck `curl -fsS http://127.0.0.1:8002/status` (interval 30s, timeout 5s, retries 3, start_period 120s, start_interval 2s), and the volume `valhalla-data` (name `overland_valhalla-data`) mounted at /custom_files with `volume.subpath: tilesets/${VALHALLA_TILESET:-none}`. A compose contract test pins each of these.

Networks: `routing` is `internal: true`; `planner` and `planner-perf` are on `[edge, routing]`; nothing but `planner` (on PLANNER_BIND) and `planner-perf` (127.0.0.1:18080) publishes a port; `planner` has no `depends_on`. Offline (YAML read): the only service without a profile is `planner`, `valhalla` has `profiles: [routing]`, the subpath default is `none`, and the memory caps of the serving services sum to at most 5 GiB (planner 1g + valhalla 4g, D83). In CI job 7 only (a test marked `compose`, not run locally: no Docker on the Mac): `docker compose config` without VALHALLA_TILESET parses and `config --services` without a profile lists only `planner`.

Seen through the docker shim's recorded argv: `make status`, `make logs`, `make diag`, `make uninstall`, the deploy and rollback scripts and `make perf-pi` call `docker compose` with `--env-file routing.env --profile routing` exactly when routing.env exists in the install dir, and exactly as before when it does not (this amends D166's 'every Pi target uses --env-file routing.env': the file is optional until a tileset is seeded, D239).

deploy.sh and rollback.sh: after the planner is published (and after a rollback brought the previous release back), when routing.env exists they run `planner_compose up -d valhalla` without `--wait`; a failure prints one line and never changes the exit code, the releases.log line or the planner. Offline tests: with routing.env the docker shim sees that call after the publish; without it no valhalla call is made; a failing valhalla start leaves `deploy ok`.

`make diag` output includes the valhalla container in its `docker stats` when the profile is on (it lists `$(PI_COMPOSE) ps -q`); README or the Makefile help says in one line that valhalla runs only after `make tiles-seed`.

`make purge` also removes the volume overland_valhalla-data (it removes every overland_* volume, D99): its typed-confirmation text now says that the map data (about 4.9 GB, rebuilt only by `make tiles-seed` or `make tiles-refresh`) goes too; a test pins the text.

steps.name: make tiles-seed and make spike-cleanup
steps.description: Seeds the first tileset from the SPIKE-2R files into the Valhalla volume, points routing.env at it and starts the engine; and the guarded clean-up of the spike directory. After a verified copy it writes `routing.env` with exactly `VALHALLA_TILESET=<TILESET>` (the previous file kept as routing.env.prev, D166), runs `planner_compose up -d --wait valhalla` and checks, from inside the compose network only (`docker compose exec valhalla curl ...`, nothing published), that `/status` answers with `version` 3.9.1 and a `tileset_last_modified` equal to EXPECT_TILESET_MODIFIED when that is given (the make target passes 1793560782 for the default TILESET 20261101, the value SPIKE-2R recorded, D92); a different value or version restores routing.env (and .prev) as they were, stops valhalla if it was not running before, and exits non-zero. `make spike-cleanup` runs deploy/scripts/spike-cleanup.sh on the Pi. steps.name: make tiles-refresh
steps.description: The quarterly map-data refresh as the DEVOPS procedure describes it: download and merge while serving, stop serving, build under the build cap, promote, switch routing.env, start and check, with every failure leaving the old tileset serving. Tested offline with the shims; never run by the crafter, and not run at the R2a gates (D237).
criteria: `make tiles-refresh` runs deploy/scripts/tiles-refresh.sh on the Pi. Preflight, read-only, each refusal changing nothing: the new tileset name is the UTC date <YYYYMMDD>, and it is refused when `tilesets/<YYYYMMDD>` already exists or equals the VALHALLA_TILESET of routing.env or routing.env.prev (a served or rollback tileset is never overwritten); disk free >= 25 GB; MemAvailable >= build cap + 1 GiB; no plan job running (the planner's /api/diagnostics through `curl_planner`).

While serving continues: `valhalla-fetch` downloads the five Geofabrik extracts into `build/src` and merges them with osmium into `build/alps.osm.pbf` (its caps: cpus 2, 6g, oom_score_adj 500; MemAvailable >= 7 GiB is checked again just before the merge). Then `planner_compose stop valhalla`, the tile build in `valhalla-build`, and the deltas of deploy/valhalla/valhalla.overrides.json applied to the built valhalla.json with jq inside the Valhalla image.

Any failure up to here (download, merge, build, overrides): valhalla is started again on the old tileset (`up -d valhalla`), routing.env is untouched, tiles.log gets `refresh failed` with the stage, exit non-zero.

Promote and switch: the four files move to `tilesets/<YYYYMMDD>/` with SHA256SUMS and `build/` is deleted; routing.env -> routing.env.prev, the new VALHALLA_TILESET, `up -d --wait valhalla`, `/status` version 3.9.1. If the start or the check fails: routing.env and .prev are restored, valhalla is started on the old tileset, the new directory is kept for inspection, tiles.log gets `refresh failed (switch)`, exit non-zero.

Only after the switch passed: tilesets other than the new and the previous one are deleted, and tiles.log gets `refresh ok` with the new tileset_last_modified. The script prints the follow-ups: `make contract-live` and one `make acceptance-pi` (D95).

Offline tests through the shims cover: each preflight refusal (existing target, disk, memory, running job), the call order of the happy path, a build failure, a failed switch (pointers restored, old tileset serving, nothing pruned), the prune only after success. `make lint-ci` passes. The Makefile help says: about 40 minutes without routing, only at a start time the owner names.

steps.name: The routing port of slice 06a: profile, typed errors, off-network places; legs keyed by road map and profile
steps.description: Extends the RoutingProvider port (D243), keys the in-memory leg cache by provider id, profile and pair (D244), and teaches the planner that a place the road map cannot snap has no Confirmed road for this plan and is asked again next time (D245). The offline road map learns to script such places.
criteria: The port (application/ports/routing_provider.py) declares `provider_id`, `profile`, `matrix(sources, targets, observer=None)` whose cells are a RoadMeasure, `None` or an `OffNetwork` (which names the end or ends of the pair the road map cannot snap), the observer protocol (`retried()`), and the errors `RoutingProviderError` with `ProviderUnreachable`, `ProviderUnavailable`, `ProviderRejected`; `OffNetwork` lives in domain/routing/road_leg.py. mypy strict passes with the offline road map and every test double.

LegResolver keeps legs per `(provider_id, profile, pair)`: a property test over two road maps that differ in provider id or in profile shows that a leg answered by one is never served to the other, and that the same road map asked twice is asked once.

An off-network cell counts as found for the request (new + cached = total holds), is in the returned table as a pair with no road, and is not kept: the next request asks about that place again while every answered pair is served from the cache. Within ONE request the resolver remembers the places a cell named off the network and answers the later pairs from or to them itself, without asking the road map (so one far place costs one extra question, not one per origin); nothing of that memory outlives the request. Property test over projects with 0 to 3 far places.

The offline road map: `profile` is `mock.v1`; a MOCK_PLAN script may list `off_network: [[lat, lon], ...]` (points matched at 6 decimals; every pair from or to such a point answers an `OffNetwork` naming that point; a malformed list is InvalidRoadMapError naming the path); the probe proves one listed point answers so. `provider_id` of a script without the new key is unchanged.

Scenario 'A place far from any road fails the plan and names it' passes with `--run-pending=slice-06a`: the run is Failed `unreachable`, its report names the POI, run #4 and the items are unchanged, and a second Recalculate asks the road map about that place again (the job's legs_new counts those pairs again, the others are cached).

steps.name: The Valhalla adapter answers matrix questions from the engine's recorded answers
steps.description: ValhallaRoutingProvider (httpx): reads /status for its identity, asks /sources_to_targets with the 4x4 costing and the snap cutoff, reads cells and null cells, and splits a batch above the pair limit into calls the engine accepts, at most two at a time. criteria: `provider_id` is `valhalla:<version>:<tileset_last_modified>` from `/status`, read on first use and after every probe; `profile` is `4x4.v1`. With the recorded status the id is `valhalla:3.9.1:1793560782`.

A matrix question posts exactly the recorded request shape (`matrix_confirmed_5x5.json`: sources and targets with `search_cutoff` = CONFIRMED_SNAP_M, `costing: auto`, the `4x4.v1` costing options of ADR-013 section 2) and reads each cell: distance in km to whole metres, time to whole seconds, both at least 1 for distinct points; a null cell is `None`. Checked cell for cell against `matrix_confirmed_5x5.json` and `matrix_confirmed_with_island_null_row.json` (every cell of the island row `None`, no other cell affected).

A batch of more than VALHALLA_MAX_MATRIX_PAIRS (default 2500) cells is asked as rectangular sub-batches of at most that many cells (targets split, `floor(max / sources)` per call; sources split too when one source row alone exceeds it), at most VALHALLA_CONCURRENCY (default 2) calls at a time through one process-wide semaphore shared by every call of the adapter (D133); the answer has the shape of the question. A property test over batch sizes proves: every cell answered once, no call above the limit, never more than two calls in flight.

Contract scenarios pass against the recorded answers: 'A Torino to Susa connection is read as one Confirmed leg', 'A missing matrix answer confirmed by a route check means no connection at that level', 'A large trip is asked in batches the routing engine accepts'.

steps.name: The Valhalla adapter tells failures from missing roads: retries, typed errors, off-network places, probe
steps.description: Client policy and error mapping of ADR-013 section 6 and Amendment 4: retry only what may pass, map what does not to typed errors, never record a failure as a missing road; the 170 flow for a place the engine cannot snap; the probe with its three not-ok reasons.
criteria: Retry only on 5xx, connect errors and timeouts: 3 attempts with waits 0.5, 1, 2 s plus jitter (the sleep is injected, tests never wait); never on 4xx. After the retries a connect error or timeout raises ProviderUnreachable, a 5xx ProviderUnavailable. Each retried call tells the observer `retried()` once. A property test over scripted answer sequences proves the attempt counts and the error raised.

Error 170 for a batch: the adapter locates the batch's points (`/locate`, verbose, the same cutoff and costing), asks again without those with no edge and answers their cells with an `OffNetwork` naming them. It keeps no memory of such places beyond the one `matrix` call (D245 as amended: the planner asks again at the next Recalculate; the resolver spares the repeats inside one request): a second call with the same place asks the engine again. When no located point explains the 170, or the engine answers 150 or any other 4xx, it raises ProviderRejected naming the engine's error code. No failure path ever yields `None`.

`probe()`: `/status` with the expected version, then the 2x2 matrix of Torino (45.0703, 7.6869) and Susa (45.1370, 7.0500) with every off-diagonal cell a positive measure. Outcomes: `ok`; degraded-healthy `routing_engine_unreachable` (connect error or timeout, no retry wait in a probe beyond one attempt), `routing_engine_not_ready` (5xx, an unreadable answer, a null or zero cell), `routing_engine_version_mismatch: found <v>, expected <e>`. A probe is never fatal, never tells the observer and updates `provider_id` when it reads a status.

Contract scenarios pass against the recorded answers: 'One place the routing engine cannot snap never removes the other places' legs' (`matrix_170_unsnappable_location_kills_call.json` + `locate_far_point_empty_edges_cutoff250.json`), 'The contract checks stop when the engine is not the version they were recorded against' and the three examples of 'Routing engine failures are reported as failures, never as missing roads'. Each loses `@pending` here. The hiccup scenario is bound in 09-05, where the plan is marked as retried; here a unit test proves the observer hears one retry and the answer is the recorded one.

steps.name: An engine failure during the look-up ends the job, stores no run and keeps the legs answered; the offline road map can fail on script
steps.description: The offline road map gets its fault plan (brief section 6), so engine failures are testable offline and it reports them as the engine does. A plan job whose road look-up fails ends `failed` with the engine's reason and words, stores no run and changes nothing; the legs answered before the failure are served from the cache next time.
criteria: MOCK_PLAN `faults`: `fail_after_pairs: N` with `kind: unreachable|unavailable` (once N pairs have been answered over the road map's life, every later call raises the typed error) and `fail_once_on_call: k` with `kind` (call number k raises once inside the road map and is retried: the caller gets the answer and the observer hears `retried()`); the probe is never failed nor counted; a malformed plan is InvalidRoadMapError. `provider_id` of a script without `faults` is unchanged.

A job whose look-up raises ProviderUnreachable ends `failed`, reason `routing_engine_unreachable`, message 'Routing engine unreachable - nothing was changed. Try again later.'; ProviderUnavailable ends `failed`, reason `routing_engine_not_ready`, message 'Routing engine not ready - nothing was changed. Try again shortly.'; ProviderRejected ends `failed` with the existing failed message. In each case no plan run is stored, the project's revision, items and runs are unchanged, one `routing.engine.error` line names the error class and reason, the `plan_job_log` row carries the reason, and the job's legs_new counts the legs answered before the failure.
The job notes `retried` (true when the observer heard a retry) and the poll payload shows `retried` and `second_pass_pairs` (brief section 5 field table); `plan_job_log.retried` is filled.

Scenario 'Road legs found before the routing engine failed are kept for next time' passes with `--run-pending=slice-06a`, with these exact numbers: the project of plan run #4 has at least 5 Included items other than the anchors (the reference project has 9; if the existing 'plan run #4 ... has been computed' step builds fewer, this scenario's world adds reference places before run #4, never changing a step other scenarios use); adding the POI needs 2k + 2 new legs (k = Included items other than the anchors: Start -> POI, each item -> POI, POI -> each item, POI -> End); the road map is scripted `fail_after_pairs: 5, kind: unreachable` counted from the Recalculate (pairs answered before are not counted against it); the first five one-origin calls each answer one new leg (Start -> POI and four items -> POI), the sixth fails. The job ends failed with the unreachable words, legs_new 5. The next Recalculate (fault cleared) has legs_new = 2k + 2 - 5 and the five answered legs among legs_cached.

Contract scenario 'The offline road map reports connections and failures the same way as the routing engine' passes and loses `@pending`: the same contract steps run against the offline road map scripted as follows, and give the same typed results: Torino to Susa (a scripted pair of 56,099 m and 3,342 s, Confirmed); the island (its pairs scripted `none`: no connection, the other places untouched); the far place (`off_network`: the other places' legs answered, the place not recorded as having no connection); the three failures (`faults` with kind unreachable for 'refuses connections' and 'does not answer within the time limit', unavailable for 'keeps answering with a server error'); the hiccup (`fail_once_on_call`: answered, observer heard a retry). Not applicable to the offline road map, with the reason in the step's docstring: the 2,500-leg batch limit (it has none) and the engine version check.

Contract scenario 'A passing server hiccup is retried and the plan still counts toward the 3-minute promise' passes against the recorded answers and loses `@pending`: one 5xx then the recorded answer gives one Confirmed leg, and a plan job whose look-up heard a retry shows `retried: true` in its poll payload and its job log row and is not excluded from any count.

steps.name: Objective per project: minimise road distance (default) or road time
steps.description: A project has an objective, `distance` by default, switchable to `time`. The solver minimises road metres or road seconds from the same legs, so switching asks no new leg. Results state the objective.
criteria: Project has `objective` (`distance` | `time`), new projects `distance`; `PATCH /api/projects/{id}` takes `objective` and/or `offroad_speed_kmh` (at least one; an unknown objective or an empty body answers 422 and nothing changes); a change is one more revision, the same value changes nothing; the project resource shows `objective`. Existing rows read `distance`. Tests: the PATCH rules through the HTTP API (unknown objective and empty body answer 422 and change nothing; the same value adds no revision; both fields together) and a repository test that a project row stored before this step reads `distance`.

SolverModelBuilder takes the objective: the third criterion `c` is the arc's road metres for `distance` and its road seconds for `time` (for a retrace arc, of entry(t) -> entry(j) only), with W1 and W2 computed from the chosen `c`; the real tables carry road seconds next to road metres; TourCounts and the poll's incumbent report road metres for `distance` and road seconds for `time` (field `objective` keeps its name; the web shows km or a duration). A property test proves the order of plans is lexicographic in (Unconfirmed legs, retraces, c) for both objectives, and that the `distance` model is unchanged: the golden pin (the sha256 of the I1 and I2 cost matrices) passes untouched, and the pin gains the W1 and W2 the unchanged code gives for I1 and I2, recorded BEFORE any production change of this step and asserted after it.

The fingerprint already holds the objective: a property test shows the two objectives never share a fingerprint for a model whose metres and seconds order differently, so the memo never serves a `distance` order for `time`.

Scenarios pass with `--run-pending=slice-06a`: 'Marco switches the objective to road time' (the results state 'minimise road time'; the job's legs_new is 0) and 'New projects minimise road distance by default'. The plan-run detail has `objective` and `objective_label` ('minimise road distance' | 'minimise road time').
`uv run pytest -q -m golden_order` and tests/perf/test_golden_model_pin.py pass unchanged; fixtures/golden/** untouched.

The solver child reads only `arc_m`: its name stays (a rename is not worth the churn across the child protocol); document that for `time` its cells are seconds. Totals of a run (road km, road time) do not depend on the objective. No migration: the `objective` column exists on projects and plan_runs. If the golden order or the pin fails: STOP and report.
